previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of liver transplant, chronic kidney disease, and GERD was admitted for substernal chest pain that improved with leaning forward and had a pleuritic component. Initial evaluation revealed sinus tachycardia, positional chest pain, and EKG changes including ST elevations in leads I and aVL, but normal troponins and echocardiogram. Pericarditis was diagnosed, likely due to a viral illness masked by immunosuppression. He was treated with colchicine and aspirin, avoiding NSAIDs due to transplant and kidney status. Volume overload from recent Lasix discontinuation was managed with diuresis. Symptoms resolved rapidly, and he was discharged home on colchicine for four weeks and restarted on Lasix, with follow-up planned for transplant and pancreatic cyst monitoring.

microbiology.comments: NEGATIVE FOR CMV IgM ANTIBODY BY EIA.  INTERPRETATION:  INFECTION AT UNDETERMINED TIME.  A positive IgG result generally indicates past exposure.  Infection with CMV once contracted remains latent and may reactivate when immunity is compromised.  If current infection is suspected, submit follow-up serum in 2-3 weeks.  Greatly elevated serum protein with IgG levels >2000 mg/dl may cause  interference with CMV IgM results.
CMV DNA not detected.  Performed by PCR.  Detection Range: 600 - 100,000 copies/ml.

NO ANTIBODY TO B. BURGDORFERI DETECTED BY EIA.  Reference Range:  No antibody detected.  Negative results do not rule out B. burgdorferi infection.  Patients in early stages of infection or on antibiotic therapy may not produce  detectable levels of antibody.  Patients with clinical history and/or  symptoms suggestive of lyme disease should be retested in 2-3 weeks.
